newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-CSR mulls Tomago aluminium expansion.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-CSR mulls Tomago aluminium expansion.

text.p: Building products, aluminium and sugar group CSR Ltd said on Monday a decision on the proposed expansion of 20,000 tonnes capacity at the Tomago aluminium smelter in New South Wales would be made by the end of 1996 and its share of the costs would be about A$40 million.
"If it is to go ahead, I think a decision would be made by the end of the year," CSR managing director Geoffrey Kells told reporters after a briefing on the company's first half results.

Tomago is 36.05 percent owned by Gove Aluminum, which in turn is 70 percent owned by CSR. The other partners in the 380,000 tonnes a year smelter are Pechniney SA, Australian Mutual Provident Society and Viag Ag.

Kells said CSR was committed to full production at Tomago, despite the lower metal price. CSR's aluminium unit earlier reported a 28 percent fall in net profit before abnormals to A$29.0 million for the six months ended September 30, 1996.

"We only have one smelter, that is Tomago. Most of the other producers have a range of smelters. Tomago is a very low cost smelter, the high cost smelters are the ones that should be turned off," Kells said.
Kells said most metal's analysts are forecasting higher aluminium prices.
